title: Dev-box CPU floor: VS Code watcher excludes + Defender exclusions (environment, not app code)
description:
Fabio's dev box sits at ~42% CPU while agents work, against a normal idle of ~5%. It has forced a reboot before, so it is not a one-off. Two measured contributors, neither in app code.

FIX 1 - Windows Defender. Antimalware Service Executable measured 11.8%, the biggest single non-VS-Code line. Real-time scanning is walking the repo, the engine and the model volume. Needs an ADMIN PowerShell so it is Fabio's to run: Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath 'C:\AI\Mpi\Cubric-Vision','G:\CubricModels'. This is a real security trade, not a free win - the excluded tree downloads model weights from R2 and Hugging Face - so it is stated to Fabio rather than buried, and he may prefer to exclude only node_modules and engine/.

FIX 2 - VS Code file watchers and search over engine/, node_modules/ and .playwright-cli/. VS Code measured 16.1% across 102 processes / 6.9 GB in Fabio's Task Manager capture. Add files.watcherExclude + search.exclude to Cubric-Vision.code-workspace. That file is GITIGNORED (.gitignore:63), so this fix is LOCAL ONLY - a fresh clone or a second machine inherits none of it.

MEASUREMENT METHOD IS PART OF THE CARD. Task Manager's CPU column is a rate and misleads on a 20-core box; the honest number is a per-process CPU-TIME DELTA over a fixed window (Get-Process .CPU before/after, cumulative seconds) divided by elapsed seconds and logical cores. Re-measure after each fix with the same method instead of declaring it fixed from one glance.

Ruled out already: this session's own processes are not the resident cause - the box measured 3-4% total between steps with nothing of the session's running. The ComfyUI engine idles at 2.3% and that is normal. Fabio's Bun process (5.8%) is not ours and was absent at measurement time.

Do NOT restart or close the user's app or the engine to chase this. Do NOT re-add the sibling repos to the workspace file while editing it (CLAUDE.md documents why).
